title: Lifting a register-machine run to memory
statement: Let $A$ be a machine with memory, let $x$ be an input, let $\beta$ be a Boolean value, let $G$ be a predicate on register-machine configurations, and let $\mu$ be a memory tape and head position. Form a register machine by keeping each deterministic instruction of $A$ and replacing every other instruction by a return of $\beta$. If this register machine reaches $a'$ from $a$ in finitely many steps while $G$ holds at every configuration strictly before reaching $a'$, and the control state of $a'$ is not halted, then $A$ reaches $(a',\mu)$ from $(a,\mu)$ without changing the memory, with $G$ holding of the register-machine component and the memory remaining equal to $\mu$ at every configuration strictly before reaching the endpoint.
